newsitem.title: USA: Ennis Cosby buried at family estate in Massachusetts.
newsitem.headline: Ennis Cosby buried at family estate in Massachusetts.

text.p: Ennis William Cosby, the only son of entertainer Bill Cosby, was buried at his family's Massachusetts estate in a small private funeral on Sunday, three days after he was killed by an unidentified gunman.

Cosby's agent, Norman Brokaw, said in a statement that the famed comedian, his wife, his four daughters and Ennis Cosby's friend Phil Caputo and a companion were the only mourners in attendance at a ceremony in Shelburne Falls, Massachusetts.

Ennis Cosby, a 27-year-old Columbia University graduate student, was gunned down early on Thursday morning while changing a flat tire on a darkened roadside along a southern California freeway. He died of a single gunshot wound to the head.
Police have mounted a massive manhunt but have so far failed to capture the killer. Authorities believe robbery was the motive.
Investigators were flooded with calls on Sunday from people claiming to know something about the suspect after he was shown in composite sketch based on the description given by a witness.

The Cosby family's tragedy has resonated across a nation that has embraced the comedian as the symbol of the all-American dad. Cosby's only son was the inspiration for some of his father's most poignant television humour.

At the family's request, Ennis Cosby's body was released on Saturday from the Los Angeles County morgue following an autopsy. It was then secretly flown to western Massachusetts, where the Cosbys have been in seclusion since leaving their New York City home late on Thursday.
"The body was interred on the grounds of the estate," a family spokesman said. Following the funeral, there were no immediate plans for a public memorial service, he said.

In Los Angeles, detectives were working around the clock to follow up on new leads, which started pouring in after a drawing of a white man with a menacing stare appeared on local news broadcasts on Saturday night.

While admitting that investigators have "no real suspect at this point," police spokesman Vincent Aguirre said detectives hope the sketch of the killer -- along with a drawing of a possible second witness -- will lead to a breakthrough.
But first, Aguirre said, police must pick their way through a maze of phone tips, including those from people who insist they have had dreams that could help investigators solve the murder.

Los Angeles police at first were investigating possible resemblances in the composite sketches of Cosby's suspected killer and a gunman who seriously wounded a sheriff's deputy last month on the shores of Lake Tahoe, one of California's most popular tourist resorts.

Sketches of the suspects in both cases showed a white male with sunken cheekbones, tight lips and a narrow nose wearing a watch cap. However, Placer County sheriff's Lt. Brad Marenger said on Sunday that investigators had determined "there's no link" between the two cases.
Enlisting the public's help in solving a murder that has shocked the nation, police released a drawing based on the description provided by a woman who saw part of the attack.

The witness, a 47-year-old screenwriter, was said to be a friend who came to help Cosby change a flat tire. When a man with a pistol accosted them, she fled the scene in fear, only to return and find Cosby lying dead next to his Mercedes convertible, a source close to the investigation said.
Police said it took until Saturday to complete the sketch because the woman had been so traumatized by the slaying and by the crush of news media attention.
